newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cartel office approves coffee merger.
newsitem.headline: German cartel office approves coffee merger.

text.p: The German cartel authority on Tuesday approved the merger of coffee-roasting firms Tchibo Holding AG and Eduscho GmbH & Co KG, a spokeswoman for the Berlin-based office said.
The two companies announced last December that Tchibo intended to buy 100 percent of competitor Eduscho to form a new venture offering roasted coffee to private households.
The cartel office held talks with competing companies about the possible consequences of the move.
Eduscho in Bremen referred requests for comment to its new owner.
Tchibo Frisch-Roest-Kaffee GmbH, the coffee arm of Tchibo Holding, said it would release a statement with comments on the transaction soon.
The cartel office said the new entity would have about the same market share as market leader Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS), part of Philip Morris, estimated at around 30 percent.
The newly-merged company would also have exclusive access to tied coffee outlets in bakery stores.
But it would not be able to dominate the market because discounter Aldi would continue to provide enough competition with cheap coffee offers in order to raise its general profile among shoppers.
